tasks.title: List Completed Orders
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. List Completed Orders is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: SELECT order_id and revenue for completed orders.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: SELECT order_id and revenue for completed orders.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT order_id, revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';
tasks.explanation: A basic WHERE filter isolates the business population before analysis.

tasks.title: Find High-Value Orders
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Find High-Value Orders is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return order_id and revenue for orders with revenue >= 2000.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return order_id and revenue for orders with revenue >= 2000.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT order_id, revenue FROM orders WHERE revenue >= 2000;
tasks.explanation: Threshold filters are common for prioritization and exception analysis.

tasks.title: Top Three Orders
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Top Three Orders is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return the three largest orders by revenue.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return the three largest orders by revenue.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT order_id, revenue FROM orders ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3;
hints: LIMIT 3 returns the top three rows.
tasks.explanation: ORDER BY plus LIMIT produces a top-N view without changing the underlying data.

tasks.title: Count Orders by Status
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Count Orders by Status is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return status and COUNT(*) AS order_count grouped by status.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return status and COUNT(*) AS order_count grouped by status.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status;
tasks.explanation: Grouped counts summarize workload or business state by category.

tasks.title: Revenue by Status
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Revenue by Status is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return status and SUM(revenue) AS revenue grouped by status.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return status and SUM(revenue) AS revenue grouped by status.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT status, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY status;
tasks.explanation: Grouped sums convert row-level transactions into business totals.

tasks.title: Marketing Conversions by Channel
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Marketing Conversions by Channel is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return channel and total conversions from campaign_performance.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return channel and total conversions from campaign_performance.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT channel, SUM(conversions) AS conversions FROM campaign_performance GROUP BY channel;
tasks.explanation: Channel aggregation supports apples-to-apples campaign comparison.

tasks.title: Completed Revenue by Segment
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Completed Revenue by Segment is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Join orders to customers and return completed revenue by segment.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Join orders to customers and return completed revenue by segment.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.revenue) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;
tasks.explanation: Joins combine transactional facts with customer dimensions.

tasks.title: Conditional Order Counts
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Conditional Order Counts is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return completed_orders, refunded_orders and cancelled_orders using CASE inside aggregates.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return completed_orders, refunded_orders and cancelled_orders using CASE inside aggregates.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'refunded' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS refunded_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders;
hints: Use SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).
Create one conditional aggregate per status.
No GROUP BY is needed for one summary row.
tasks.explanation: Conditional aggregation creates multiple business KPIs in one scan.

tasks.title: Segments Above Revenue Threshold
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Segments Above Revenue Threshold is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return completed-revenue segments with SUM(revenue) > 3000.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return completed-revenue segments with SUM(revenue) > 3000.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.revenue) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.revenue) > 3000;
tasks.explanation: HAVING filters aggregated groups, unlike WHERE which filters source rows.

tasks.title: Customers Above Average Revenue
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Customers Above Average Revenue is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return customer_id and completed revenue for customers whose completed revenue is above the average customer total.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return customer_id and completed revenue for customers whose completed revenue is above the average customer total.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id, revenue FROM customer_revenue WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM customer_revenue);
hints: The comparison average must be based on those customer totals.
A subquery can produce the average of aggregates.
tasks.explanation: Nested aggregation is useful when the benchmark itself is an aggregate across groups.

tasks.title: CTE for Customer Revenue
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. CTE for Customer Revenue is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Use a CTE to calculate completed revenue per customer, then keep customers with revenue >= 2000.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Use a CTE to calculate completed revenue per customer, then keep customers with revenue >= 2000.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id, revenue FROM customer_revenue WHERE revenue >= 2000;
hints: Aggregate completed revenue inside the CTE.
tasks.explanation: CTEs make multi-step SQL easier to read and review.

tasks.title: Bucket Order Value
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Bucket Order Value is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return order_id and value_band where revenue >=2000 is High, >=1000 is Medium, otherwise Low.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return order_id and value_band where revenue >=2000 is High, >=1000 is Medium, otherwise Low.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT order_id, CASE WHEN revenue >= 2000 THEN 'High' WHEN revenue >= 1000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS value_band FROM orders;
tasks.explanation: CASE expressions translate numeric values into business-friendly categories.

tasks.title: Unique Customer Regions
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Unique Customer Regions is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return each distinct region from customers.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return each distinct region from customers.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM customers;
tasks.explanation: DISTINCT is useful for inspecting category coverage and data quality.

tasks.title: Rank Orders With Row Number
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Rank Orders With Row Number is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return order_id, revenue and ROW_NUMBER() over revenue descending as revenue_rank.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return order_id, revenue and ROW_NUMBER() over revenue descending as revenue_rank.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT order_id, revenue, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM orders;
hints: Put ORDER BY revenue DESC inside OVER().
tasks.explanation: ROW_NUMBER assigns a deterministic sequence over an ordered result set.

tasks.title: Rank Customers by Revenue
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Rank Customers by Revenue is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Aggregate completed revenue per customer, then RANK customers by revenue descending.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Aggregate completed revenue per customer, then RANK customers by revenue descending.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id, revenue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM customer_revenue;
hints: Use a CTE for customer revenue.
Order the window by revenue DESC.
tasks.explanation: Window ranking works well on an already aggregated business grain.

tasks.title: Running Completed Revenue
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Running Completed Revenue is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Aggregate completed daily revenue, then calculate cumulative revenue by date.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Aggregate completed daily revenue, then calculate cumulative revenue by date.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH daily_revenue AS (SELECT order_date, SUM(revenue) AS daily_revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY order_date) SELECT order_date, daily_revenue, SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue FROM daily_revenue;
tasks.explanation: Running totals show cumulative progress while preserving each time period.

tasks.title: Previous-Day Revenue With LAG
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Previous-Day Revenue With LAG is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return daily completed revenue and prior_day_revenue using LAG.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return daily completed revenue and prior_day_revenue using LAG.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH daily_revenue AS (SELECT order_date, SUM(revenue) AS daily_revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY order_date) SELECT order_date, daily_revenue, LAG(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS prior_day_revenue FROM daily_revenue;
tasks.explanation: LAG exposes prior-period values without a self join.

tasks.title: Three-Period Moving Average
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Three-Period Moving Average is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return order_date and a 3-row moving average of completed daily revenue rounded to one decimal.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return order_date and a 3-row moving average of completed daily revenue rounded to one decimal.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH daily_revenue AS (SELECT order_date, SUM(revenue) AS daily_revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY order_date) SELECT order_date, ROUND(AVG(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) AS moving_avg_3 FROM daily_revenue;
hints: Use ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
tasks.explanation: Moving windows smooth short-term variation while retaining time order.

tasks.title: Segment Revenue Share
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Segment Revenue Share is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return segment, completed revenue and revenue_share_pct using a window total.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return segment, completed revenue and revenue_share_pct using a window total.
tasks.expectedAnswer: WITH segment_revenue AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.revenue) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT segment, revenue, ROUND(revenue * 100.0 / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 1) AS revenue_share_pct FROM segment_revenue;
hints: Use SUM(revenue) OVER() for the denominator.
tasks.explanation: Window totals let each grouped row retain context about the overall total.

tasks.title: Rank Orders Within Segment
tasks.context: You are working in the e-commerce analyst SQL lab. Rank Orders Within Segment is the next ticket.
tasks.goal: Return segment, order_id, revenue and ROW_NUMBER within each segment by revenue descending for completed orders.
tasks.deliverable: Return exactly the requested columns and business grain.
tasks.prompt: Return segment, order_id, revenue and ROW_NUMBER within each segment by revenue descending for completed orders.
tasks.expectedAnswer: SELECT c.segment, o.order_id, o.revenue, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.segment ORDER BY o.revenue DESC) AS segment_rank FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';
hints: Order each partition by revenue DESC.
tasks.explanation: Partitioned windows rank records independently inside each business segment.
